Engine::resample + ClipResampler: EXACT ALIGNMENT. Output frame count = ceil(frames*out/in) exactly (requested == actual). Alignment derived from rubato 5.0.1 internals (start index -(SINC_LEN-1), trim floor(SINC_LEN*r/2)): rubato leaves the output ahead by 1-frac(128 r) frames (0.4..1.0 measured); the resampler prepends pad_input_frames zeros (smallest s with q | 128+s and non-negative lag) and drops drop_output_frames, giving whole-frame alignment. Pad/drop: 48k->44.1k (32,29), 44.1k->48k (19,20), 32k->48k (2,2), 48k->96k (1,1), 48k->48k (1,0). Impulse test on those five pairs: peak lands on the exact image index, residual offset 0.007..0.010 frames (about the 1/128 sinc-table step). Sinc path retained (no FFT feature, no new deps).

Engine::bounce_resampled (STU-ARC-021 over a sample-rate converter): graph pre(Processor, input rate) -> ClipResampler -> post(Processor, output rate), whole clip (input and converted clip <= MAX_BLOCK_FRAMES). ResampledBounceReceipt: requested_input_frames, requested_output_frames = ceil(in*out_rate/in_rate) in u128, actual_output_frames (sink total); the three must agree or the bounce is refused (LengthMismatch), nothing clamped/truncated/zero-padded; exact input AND output start/end samples and ticks (output start = input start*out/in must be a whole sample, else OutOfRange), ceil_excess_ticks (< 1 output sample), StageFacts [pre, resampler, post] (kind, in/out rate, in/out frames, compensated latency_samples, identity), embedded pre/post BounceReceipt + ResampleReceipt (pad/drop/trimmed_tail), graph_identity (SHA-256, scheme in docs), digest of the delivered stream. All statically decidable refusals (counts, rates, layouts, capacities, positions, finite input) happen before the first block; the sink is called only by the final stage; slot held throughout; processors reset on any failure. Hand-computed counts: 44.1k->48k 1000->1089, 44100->48000, 441->480, 1->2; 48k->44.1k 1000->919, 48000->44100, 480->441, 1->1; latency 240 @48k and round(220.5)=221 @44.1k compensated without changing counts

Streaming SRC (stream_resample.rs): ClipResampler::begin_stream(input_frames) / push_stream(planar pieces, emit) / finish_stream(emit) -> StreamReceipt / abort_stream / stream_buffer_bytes. Same rubato call sequence as Engine::resample (pad zeros first, a chunk is processed as soon as it is full, last partial chunk with partial_len, silence pumped with partial_len=Some(0); startup delay + alignment drop skipped; delivery stops at the exact integer count), so the delivered samples are BIT-IDENTICAL to the whole-clip path: proven by to_bits equality on 5 rate pairs x 53 lengths (1..40, 63..65, 1005, chunk boundaries 1023..1025, 2047..2049, 4799..4801) with pushes of 1/7/255/1000 frames and on a 4 s 44.1k->48k clip with 4096/333 pushes, plus equal counts, pad/drop/trimmed_tail/delay and peak/rms. Static refusals in begin_stream (0 frames, count overflow, converter that cannot produce the exact count); push refuses non-finite/channel/length mismatch/frames beyond the declared count; any error ends the stream and resets the converter

Block-streaming Engine::bounce_resampled: processor stages are push-style StageRunners (stage.rs: same block boundaries, latency compensation, settle gate per block and meters as Engine::bounce, BounceRun shared with bounce.rs), the converter streams between them, the sink receives output-timeline chunks as they appear; no MAX_BLOCK_FRAMES cap on clip length; ResampledBounceReceipt EQUALS the whole-clip oracle's receipt field for field except working_set_bytes (6 s 48k->44.1k, limiter latency 341 -> converter -> EQ, blocks 256 and 77, all samples to_bits equal). Engine::bounce_resampled_whole_clip keeps the previous implementation (MAX_BLOCK_FRAMES bound) as the oracle. ResampledBounceReceipt.working_set_bytes reports the bounce's own buffers: streaming 10_640 B for a mono 256-frame-block graph (staging 2 x 1024 B + converter 4096 B in + 4496 B out) independent of clip length, versus the clip buffers of the whole-clip path

output_guard.finding: Gain::new(f32::MAX) is a finite parameter and Gain(MAX) on 2.0 publishes inf (dsp.rs:82/113); ChannelMix, Equalizer (f64 filter cast to f32), RampedGain, Engine::mix, the sinc converter and the spectrum bins can overflow the same way from finite input
output_guard.decision_with_evidence: output check, not admission validation: a finite coefficient cannot bound its product with an unbounded finite sample (Gain MAX on 2.0, ChannelMix [MAX, MAX] on (1,1) and on (2,-2) = NaN, EQ +48 dB on 1e37, ramp to MAX on 4.0, mix of two MAX sends, a +/-MAX alternating clip through the 2x sinc, square-wave spectrum bin 1.2071068*A), so only a scan of the produced samples is sound. Cost: one branch-free pass (64-sample folded finite test, early exit per group) per processed block, comparable to the peak/rms pass BlockReceipt::measure already makes; no allocation
output_guard.placement: Engine::run_block after process and settle (a canceled or stale block is not scanned), error path = discard unpublished + proc.reset() (RampedGain restores its pre-block gain, tested); Chain scans each intermediate stage so a later limiter cannot clamp an infinity into plausible full-scale output and a short block is not hidden by the limiter's 341-sample delay; Engine::mix, Engine::resample (published region after the alignment shift), StreamState chunk (before emit and meters) and SpectrumAnalyzer::analyze (bins)
